html:
SMTO-PSM-0001 — SMTO couldn't use the @ parameters in your request

GUID: 0be3f314-b545-4b32-88a8-1167e33d4c13
Slug: parameter-reference-invalid
Domain: PSM · Subsystem: psm

What happened

  • One or more Parameter Store entries you mentioned with @ couldn't be read or attached, so SMTO stopped before the Agent started on your request. Your saved parameters weren't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the message names a parameter with an invalid value, open Parameter Store, select it, open the Value tab, select Reveal & edit value, fix the value and select Save. SMTO can only attach a parameter whose saved value it can read correctly.
  2. If the message mentions a character limit, mention fewer parameters in one request, or shorten the values and descriptions saved in them. All the @ parameters in one request must fit together within a size limit.
  3. If the message says the task uses an older format or must be resubmitted, send your request again as a new message instead of resuming the old task. An older saved task can't be resumed this way, but a new message is captured fresh.
  4. If the message says the Parameter Store is disabled or unavailable, ask the person who manages SMTO to turn it on or check SMTO's saved data. Without the Parameter Store, SMTO can't look up any @ parameter.

What success looks like

  • Your request starts and the Agent's reply uses the parameters you mentioned.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't type passwords or other secrets straight into your message to work around this; keep them in the Parameter Store.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Parameter reference resolution rejected the request before inference: the Parameter Store was disabled or unreadable, a referenced record held invalid JSON, the expansion exceeded agent_parameter_prompt_max_chars, or the task's accepted parameter snapshot was invalid or in a legacy format.

What this means

  • ParameterReferenceError is the shared pre-inference rejection for invalid/missing references, unavailable storage, oversized/invalid context or an unsupported accepted snapshot. Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.

Why this can happen

  • ParameterReferenceError is the shared pre-inference rejection for invalid/missing references, unavailable storage, oversized/invalid context or an unsupported accepted snapshot.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the more specific reference reason and exact accepted key/revision instead of assuming a missing record.

How to fix it

  • Read the ResolutionDiagnostic reason in Technical details (disabled, store_missing, lookup_failed, invalid_json, invalid_record, oversized, legacy_snapshot, invalid_snapshot or usage_failed). Fix the named record's value, reduce the referenced entries or raise agent_parameter_prompt_max_chars, enable agent_parameter_store_enabled or restore the store, or submit a new task instead of resuming a stale or legacy snapshot.
  • Correct the specific reference/snapshot problem through the supported Parameter Store flow while preserving accepted private revisions.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended references resolve under the current supported snapshot contract.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
